title: HELIX Terminology: Learning/Training Type
description: Categories of professional development and training activities for institutional employees.

codes.definition: Credit or non-credit course taken at the institution or elsewhere, often under the tuition waiver benefit. May count toward a degree, certificate, or professional credential.

Structured, interactive training session, typically 2-8 hours. May be offered by HR, the teaching center, IT, or an external provider. Common topics: Banner navigation, budget management, inclusive teaching practices.
Program leading to a professional credential (e.g., PMP, SHRM-CP, CPA continuing education, CITI research ethics). Institution may fund exam fees and preparation materials.

Professional conference attendance, including presentation or attendance. Funded through professional development budgets. Requires travel authorization and post-travel reporting at most institutions.
Online synchronous training session. May be recorded for asynchronous viewing. Increasingly common for compliance training (Title IX, FERPA, cybersecurity awareness).

Asynchronous online learning modules accessed through the LMS or external platform (LinkedIn Learning, Coursera, etc.). Often used for compliance training with completion tracking and certificate generation.
Structured learning occurring during normal work through observation, shadowing, job rotation, or stretch assignments. Typically documented in the performance management system.
Formal or informal pairing of experienced and less-experienced employees for professional growth. May be part of new employee onboarding, leadership development, or faculty development programs.

Required training for regulatory compliance: Title IX, FERPA, GLBA information security, Clery Act, hazardous materials, conflict of interest, responsible conduct of research, driver safety. Non-completion may trigger hold on system access or pay.
